purpose: Independent geocentric lunar geometry test reference; no crop-effect validation.

source.name: NASA/JPL Horizons observer table

frames.declination_deg: Airless apparent equator/equinox of date, EOP-corrected IAU76/80; light-time, deflection, aberration, precession and nutation included.
frames.distance_au: Apparent light-time-corrected geocentric range in AU.
frames.radial_velocity_km_s: Apparent geocentric range-rate; positive receding, negative approaching.
frames.ecliptic_coordinates: Apparent observer-centred IAU76/80 ecliptic of date; light-time, deflection and aberration included.
frames.iau_constellation: IAU 1930 region containing the ASTROMETRIC target-centre position, as supplied by Horizons quantity 29.

precision.time_tags: UTC hourly samples printed to the minute.
precision.event_output: Numerical spline root rounded to nearest second; not independent one-second physical accuracy.

source.time_caveat: Horizons UT output after 1962 is UTC; future intervals use the last known leap-second offset at retrieval.

method.interpolation: SciPy CubicSpline with not-a-knot boundary conditions, continuous hourly inputs, no extrapolation.
method.nodes: Roots of interpolated apparent ecliptic latitude; increasing latitude is ascending node.
method.apsides: Roots of interpolated JPL deldot range-rate; negative-to-positive is perigee, positive-to-negative apogee.
method.declination_turns: Roots of the derivative of the interpolated apparent equatorial declination; classify with second derivative.
method.coordinates: Direct source values at 12:00 UTC on the 15th of each month; no interpolation.
method.constellations: Every adjacent hourly sample pair whose JPL IAU code changes; each pair is a one-hour ingress bracket, not an exact ingress time.

limits: Interpolating an hourly table does not create authoritative second-resolution event measurements.
Apparent coordinates and Horizons astrometric constellation labels have different corrections; tiny ingress offsets can be frame effects.
A constellation excursion shorter than an hour can be missed if both sample endpoints have the same label.
Geocentric events do not provide local rise/set, culmination altitude, eclipse visibility or occultation circumstances.
No hemisphere-dependent agricultural interpretation or publisher-specific sector boundary is tested by these fixtures.
Agreement verifies astronomical computation only, not planting, harvest, flavour or yield claims.
